title: Emit structured perf log events for benchmark ingestion (phase breakdown, GPU clocks, kernel IDs)
author: Julian Moore
release_notes: - Adds optional structured perf log events (JSONL) for benchmark ingestion, including per-phase timings (prefill/decode), GPU clock snapshots, and kernel identifiers. Disabled by default; enable via runtime flag/config for perf-lab and canaries.
description: Context: During the FP8/INT8 benchmarking sprint we need repeatable, machine-readable perf artifacts from the runtime to (a) attribute regressions to prefill vs decode, (b) correlate tail latency with GPU clock drift / power state changes, and (c) track which kernel family/variant was actually selected for the critical ops. Today we only have human-oriented log lines + ad-hoc tracing spans; benchmark-lab ingestion (and upcoming report generation) needs a stable schema and tags. What this PR does: Adds a structured perf log event sink that emits JSONL records at the end of each request and (optionally) per-phase. The event includes: request_id, model_id, quant_mode (fp16/fp8/int8), runtime_version/commit, gpu (sku, uuid), gpu_clocks (sm_clock_mhz, mem_clock_mhz, power_w, temp_c when available), phase breakdown (ttft_ms, prefill_ms, decode_ms, queue_wait_ms, scheduler_overhead_ms), token counts (prompt_tokens, completion_tokens), and selected kernel IDs for major op classes (attention_prefill, attention_decode, gemm) plus representative shapes (m,n,k; seq_len; head_dim) and a stable kernel_family string. The sink is gated behind `--perf_log_json` (or `RUNTIME_PERF_LOG_JSON=1`) and writes to existing perf-lab log directory (or stdout when configured) as one line per event to keep ingestion simple. Design notes: (1) Overhead: emission occurs after response completion and avoids per-token logging; NVML reads are cached per-process with a configurable sampling interval. (2) Stability: schema versioned with `schema_version: 1` and `event_type` set to `runtime.perf.request_summary` (and `runtime.perf.phase_summary` when enabled). (3) Safety: if NVML is unavailable, fields are omitted and `gpu_clock_source` is set to `unavailable` rather than failing the request path. (4) Kernel IDs: we plumb the kernel selector’s chosen implementation into a stable string ID and numeric `kernel_id` when available; no pointers / raw addresses. Testing: adds unit tests for JSON encoding + schema presence; integration test uses a fake NVML provider; golden JSON fixtures live under `runtime/tests/data/perf_events/`. Docs: updates runtime config docs to describe flags and shows an example event for benchmark-lab ingestion. Follow-ups (not in this PR): benchmark-lab will standardize metadata tags across repos (see PRs in benchmark-lab), and perf-canary will begin collecting these records nightly once gating thresholds land. Example event (abbrev): `{"schema_version":1,"event_type":"runtime.perf.request_summary","ts_unix_ms":1760123456789,"request_id":"...","model_id":"qwen2.5-32b-instruct","quant_mode":"int8","gpu":{"sku":"H100-SXM","uuid":"GPU-..."},"gpu_clocks":{"sm_clock_mhz":1410,"mem_clock_mhz":3201,"power_w":412.3},"timing_ms":{"ttft":182.4,"prefill":155.2,"decode":923.8,"queue_wait":12.1},"tokens":{"prompt":2048,"completion":512},"kernels":{"attention_prefill":{"family":"flashattn_fp8_v3","id":"fa_fp8_v3_t128"},"gemm":{"family":"cutlass_int8_gemm","id":"ct_i8_sm90_128x128"}}}`

review_conversation: Noah Patel: The overall shape looks good. Two asks: (1) Please clarify whether timing uses monotonic or wall clock. Ingestion needs consistent semantics for comparing across runs. (2) For kernel IDs, can we ensure the string is stable across builds and not derived from enum ordering? Julian Moore (author): Updated docs + field names: `ts_unix_ms` is wall clock for correlation; all durations are derived from monotonic clock. Also changed kernel IDs to be explicit string constants registered by the selector (`kernel_family` + `kernel_impl_id`) rather than enum ordinals; numeric `kernel_id` is optional and only used for internal correlation. Allison Grant: Can we include tags for `runtime_commit` and `container_digest` so dashboards can filter precisely? Also, please avoid emitting empty objects for gpu_clocks when NVML is missing (makes queries noisy). Julian Moore (author): Added `runtime_commit` (already available) and `build.container_digest` when stamping is enabled; omitted empty objects and set `gpu_clock_source`. Sean Gallagher: NVML reads can be slow / flaky on busy nodes. Please keep sampling interval configurable and default to something conservative. Also, ensure failure to read NVML never blocks request completion. Julian Moore (author): Added `--perf_log_gpu_telemetry_interval_ms` default 1000ms, and reads are best-effort with timeout; errors increment a counter and fields are omitted. Connor O'Brien: For release train: is this behind a flag and off by default? I don’t want accidental log volume surprises. Julian Moore (author): Yes, entirely off by default; perf-lab enables via config. Added a short note to release notes and confirmed log line size is bounded. Rina Kobayashi: Please add a minimal example in docs that benchmark-lab can parse; also would be helpful if the file naming includes model/gpu/quant tags. Julian Moore (author): Added example + recommended naming convention; actual filename template remains controlled by perf-lab harness but includes tags in the event. Approvals: Noah Patel approved after ID stability change; Allison Grant approved after tag additions; Sean Gallagher approved after telemetry caching; Connor O'Brien approved with flag gating note; Rina Kobayashi approved after docs example.
